title: Locally constant simplicial presheaves and spaces over a nerve
statement:
Use simplicial sets, nerves, spaces and derived mapping spaces as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and projective simplicial-presheaf model structures and left Bousfield localization as in [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-localization-comparison]. Let $C$ be a small ordinary category in a universe enlarged to contain all presheaves considered. Write $h_x(y)=\operatorname{Hom}_C(y,x)$, regarded as a discrete simplicial set. Let $P_{\mathrm{lc}}(C)$ be the left Bousfield localization of $\operatorname{Fun}(C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{sSet})$ at all maps $h_x\to h_{x'}$ induced by arrows $x\to x'$ in $C$. Its fibrant objects are precisely the objectwise Kan presheaves sending all arrows to weak homotopy equivalences. For a simplicial presheaf $F$ define
$$\mathcal N_C(F)_n=\coprod_{c_0\to\cdots\to c_n}F(c_n)_n.$$
The map to $NC$ forgets the last coordinate. Faces other than the last delete or compose the corresponding arrow and apply the matching simplicial face to the last coordinate; the last face also restricts along $c_{n-1}\to c_n$; degeneracies insert identities and apply simplicial degeneracies. This is left adjoint to
$$\mathcal S_C(T)(x)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathsf{sSet}/NC}(N(C/x),T),$$
where the displayed simplicial mapping object has $n$-simplices maps $N(C/x)\times\Delta^n\to T$ over $NC$, and $C/x$ is the category of arrows to $x$. The adjunction is a simplicial Quillen equivalence between $P_{\mathrm{lc}}(C)$ and the slice of the Kan-Quillen model category over $NC$. In particular, its derived mapping-space comparison is
$$\operatorname{Map}^{h}_{P_{\mathrm{lc}}(C)}(h_y,h_x)\simeq\operatorname{Map}^{h}_{\mathsf{sSet}/NC}(N(C/y),N(C/x)).$$
These are the comparisons induced by the stated adjunction; they respect representable morphisms, identities, composition and the associated homotopies. For a fibrant presheaf $F$, evaluation gives $\operatorname{Map}^{h}_{P_{\mathrm{lc}}(C)}(h_y,F)\simeq F(y)$.

source.place: Appendix A, Proposition A.0.3 and its proof, printed pp. 207-208 (PDF pp. 214-215); enriched evaluation is the projective simplicial Yoneda formula Read online; not archived locally. No Stacks tag states this simplicial homotopy-theoretic result.

proof.text: Put $A_x=N(C/x)$ over $NC$. Degreewise co-Yoneda gives $\int^{x\in C}h_x\times F(x)\cong F$: the pair $(a:y\to x,z\in F(x)_n)$ goes to $F(a)z$, with inverse represented by $(1_y,z)$. Likewise $\int^x A_x\times F(x)$ has degree-$n$ representatives $(c_0\to\cdots\to c_n\to x,z)$, identified with $(c_0\to\cdots\to c_n,F(c_n\to x)z)$. This is exactly $\mathcal N_C(F)$ with the stated operators. The coend universal property gives the enriched adjunction with $\mathcal S_C(T)(x)=\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{/NC}(A_x,T)$, in each simplicial degree as well as on vertices. In particular $\mathcal N_C(h_x)=A_x$ and $\mathcal N_C(F\times K)=\mathcal N_C(F)\times K$. Enriched Yoneda is explicit: a natural map $h_y\times\Delta^n\to F$ is determined by its value on $1_y$, giving the isomorphism $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(h_y,F)\cong F(y)$. The inverse sends $(a:z\to y,t)$ to $F(a)(s(t))$ for the selected simplex $s:\Delta^n\to F(y)$.

source.place: Appendix A, proof of Proposition A.0.3, printed pp. 207-208 (PDF pages 214-215).

proof.text: By [lem-coef-model-over-structure] and [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], $\mathsf{sSet}/NC$ has the stated slice model structure, including when $NC$ is not Kan, and every object of this slice is cofibrant. It is simplicial with the mapping objects in the statement: a lifting problem for a mapping-object map against a boundary or horn is adjoint to the corresponding pushout-product lifting problem for the underlying cofibration and fibration in $\mathsf{sSet}$. The Cartesian simplicial-model axiom for $\mathsf{sSet}$ in [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model] supplies the lift, also in the slice since the original square is over $NC$. The projective generating maps from that same node are carried by $\mathcal N_C$ to $A_x\times\partial\Delta^n\to A_x\times\Delta^n$ and $A_x\times\Lambda_i^n\to A_x\times\Delta^n$. They are respectively cofibrations and trivial cofibrations by the Cartesian simplicial-model axiom. The coend formula preserves colimits and retracts, so $\mathcal N_C\dashv\mathcal S_C$ is projectively Quillen. The maps $\varnothing\to h_x$ are generating cofibrations, so each $h_x$ is projectively cofibrant.

source.place: Appendix A, proof of Proposition A.0.3, printed pp. 207-208 (PDF pages 214-215).

proof.text: The object $1_x$ is terminal in $C/x$. The unique arrows to it give a natural transformation from the identity to the constant functor at $1_x$. By [lem-coef-nerve-natural-homotopy-equivalence], $A_x$ is contractible, and $\{x\}\to A_x$ is a weak equivalence and a monomorphism over $NC$. Every arrow $a:x\to x'$ induces a weak equivalence $A_x\to A_{x'}$, since both spaces are contractible. For a fibrant slice object $T\to NC$, the mapping-space formula of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] therefore shows that $\mathcal S_C(T)(x)$ is Kan and that $\mathcal S_C(T)(x')\to\mathcal S_C(T)(x)$ is a weak equivalence. Moreover restriction along $\{x\}\to A_x$ is a trivial Kan fibration $\mathcal S_C(T)(x)\to T_x$ by the slice simplicial-model axiom of step 2. Thus $\mathcal S_C(T)$ is local fibrant. Here is the precise localization fibrancy check. Factor each representable arrow $h_x\to h_{x'}$ in the projective model as a cofibration $i_a:h_x\to M_a$ followed by a trivial fibration $M_a\to h_{x'}$. Both endpoints of $i_a$ are cofibrant. By the mapping-space formula of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], the derived local tests for $i_a$ and the original representable arrow agree. The small family of $i_a$ therefore has the same local objects and local equivalences as the family in the statement. Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-bousfield-model-structure] to this family in the left proper combinatorial simplicial projective model of step 2. It supplies the localized simplicial model with unchanged cofibrations and precisely the original fibrant local objects. Its weak equivalences are the prescribed local equivalences, so it is the model $P_{\mathrm{lc}}(C)$ in the statement. By the enriched Yoneda calculation in step 1, its fibrant objects are exactly the objectwise Kan presheaves inverting all arrows. In particular the presheaves $\mathcal S_C(T)$ just constructed are localized fibrant.

source.place: Appendix A, proof of Proposition A.0.3, printed pp. 207-208 (PDF pages 214-215).

proof.text: The localization leaves the projective cofibrations unchanged by the application of [lem-coef-simplicial-bousfield-model-structure] in step 3. The class of projectively fibrant local objects is closed under objectwise weak equivalences between projectively fibrant objects: the defining derived mapping-space tests are invariant under such weak equivalences by [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. Let $i:F\to G$ be a cofibration and a local equivalence. For every fibrant slice object $T$, step 3 makes $\mathcal S_C(T)$ fibrant local. By [lem-coef-cofibration-local-mapping-test], $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(i,\mathcal S_C(T))$ is a trivial Kan fibration, without any cofibrancy assumption on $F,G$. By step 1 this equals $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{/NC}(\mathcal N_C(i),T)$. All slice objects are cofibrant, so by [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] these are the derived mapping-space tests of $\mathcal N_C(i)$. On components they show that precomposition by $\mathcal N_C(i)$ gives bijections of Hom sets into every object of the slice homotopy category (each has a fibrant representative). Write $f=q\mathcal N_C(i):X\to Y$ in that homotopy category. Surjectivity of $f^*:\operatorname{Hom}(Y,X)\to\operatorname{Hom}(X,X)$ gives $g:Y\to X$ with $gf=1_X$. Since $(fg)f=f=1_Yf$, injectivity of $f^*:\operatorname{Hom}(Y,Y)\to\operatorname{Hom}(X,Y)$ gives $fg=1_Y$. Thus $f$ is invertible. By [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences], $\mathcal N_C(i)$ is a weak equivalence. It is already a cofibration by step 2. Hence the given simplicial adjunction is Quillen for the localized model as well.

source.place: Appendix A, proof of Proposition A.0.3, printed pp. 207-208 (PDF pages 214-215).

proof.text: Here is the homotopy-fiber argument left implicit in HAGII. For an arrow-inverting presheaf $F$ form the simplicial diagram of spaces $E_n=\coprod_{c_0\to\cdots\to c_n}qF(c_n)$ and the discrete simplicial diagram $B_n=\coprod_{c_0\to\cdots\to c_n}*$. These disjoint unions agree with the images under $q$ of the disjoint unions of simplicial sets: all simplicial sets are cofibrant, and enriched maps from a disjoint union into a Kan complex form the product of the individual mapping Kan complexes. The mapping-space formula of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] therefore verifies the coherent coproduct universal property directly. For a monotone map $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, the fiber over a string in $B_n$ of the naturality square is the map $qF(c_n)\to qF(c_{\alpha(m)})$ induced by the composite $c_{\alpha(m)}\to c_n$. It is an equivalence, so this square is a pullback of spaces: both sides decompose over that discrete indexing set. By [lem-coef-space-geometric-descent], $E_0\to|E_\bullet|$ over $B_0\to|B_\bullet|$ is a pullback square. By [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-space-colimit], the two realizations, with these maps, are $q\mathcal N_C(F)$ and $qNC$. Pulling the square back along $\{x\}\to B_0$ therefore identifies the canonical map from $qF(x)$ to the homotopy fiber of $q\mathcal N_C(F)\to qNC$ at $x$ as an equivalence. This is a statement about that canonical inclusion, not an unspecified equivalence of spaces. No assumption that $NC$ is Kan has been made.

source.place: Theorem 6.1.3.9(4) and Corollary A.2.9.30 / Example A.2.9.31; explicit application to the simplicial replacement in HAGII Appendix A, Proposition A.0.3.

proof.text: We spell out the comparison with strict fibers even over the possibly non-Kan base $B=NC$. If $T\to B$ is a Kan fibration, choose a trivial cofibration $B\to RB$ with $RB$ Kan and factor $T\to RB$ as a weak equivalence $T\to\widehat T$ followed by a fibration. Then $\widehat T$ is Kan. By right properness in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], $B\times_{RB}\widehat T\to\widehat T$ is a weak equivalence. Hence $T\to B\times_{RB}\widehat T$ is a weak equivalence between Kan fibrations over $B$. By [lem-coef-kan-fibration-arbitrary-base-fibers], its strict-fiber maps are weak equivalences. Since $RB$ and $\widehat T$ are Kan, the homotopy-pullback clause of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] identifies $\widehat T_x$ with the homotopy fiber of $qT\to qB$ at $x$. Consequently $T_x$ computes that homotopy fiber, naturally in $T$ and with the map from any object mapping into $T$ over $B$. Functorial factorizations make all the squares used here natural. This justifies applying the conclusion of step 5 to a slice fibrant replacement of $\mathcal N_C(F)$.

source.place: Appendix A, proof of Proposition A.0.3, printed pp. 207-208 (PDF pages 214-215).

proof.text: For an objectwise weak equivalence $F\to G$, apply [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] to the bisimplicial sets $\coprod_{c_0\to\cdots\to c_n}F(c_n)_m$ and its analogue for $G$. In each fixed $n$ the map is a coproduct of weak equivalences, hence a weak equivalence: its realization is a disjoint union, so the component and based homotopy-group conditions are checked on each summand. Thus $\mathcal N_C(F)\to\mathcal N_C(G)$ is a weak equivalence. In particular for a local fibrant $F$ and projective cofibrant replacement $QF\to F$, the maps $\mathcal N_C(QF)\to\mathcal N_C(F)$ are weak equivalences. So $\mathbf L\mathcal N_C(F)$ is represented by $\mathcal N_C(F)$ itself. Choose a slice fibrant replacement $\mathcal N_C(F)\to T$. By [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], the derived unit is computed by $QF\to\mathcal S_C(T)$, adjoint to $\mathcal N_C(QF)\to\mathcal N_C(F)\to T$, after inverting $QF\to F$. Define $u_F:F\to\mathcal S_C(T)$ to be adjoint to $\mathcal N_C(F)\to T$. Naturality of the ordinary adjunction says exactly that the preceding map from $QF$ is $u_F\circ(QF\to F)$. Hence $u_F$ represents the derived unit without requiring $F$ to be projectively cofibrant. Its value at $x$, followed by the restriction $\mathcal S_C(T)(x)\to T_x$ of step 3, is precisely the canonical map $F(x)\to T_x$: in degree $n$, the unit sends $z\in F(x)_n$ to the map on $A_x\times\Delta^n$ whose value on a chain ending in $c\to x$ is $F(c\to x)z$ with the matching simplicial restriction. Restricting to the identity chain gives $z$ itself. Steps 5 and 6 say that this map to $T_x$ is a weak equivalence; step 3 says the restriction from $\mathcal S_C(T)(x)$ is a weak equivalence. Thus the derived unit is objectwise a weak equivalence, hence is an equivalence in the localized model. Every object has a local fibrant replacement, so the derived unit is an equivalence everywhere.

source.place: Appendix A, proof of Proposition A.0.3, printed pp. 207-208 (PDF pages 214-215).

proof.text: The right derived functor is conservative. Represent a map in the slice homotopy category by a map $u:T\to T'$ between fibrant slice objects; such representatives exist after cofibrant and fibrant replacement by [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], and all slice objects are cofibrant. If $\mathbf R\mathcal S_C(u)$ is an equivalence, mapping out of the cofibrant $h_x$ in the localized model and using step 1 shows $\mathcal S_C(u)(x)$ is an equivalence for every $x$. The restriction weak equivalences of step 3 identify these maps with $u_x:T_x\to T'_x$. By [lem-coef-kan-fibration-arbitrary-base-fibers], $u$ is a weak equivalence over $NC$. Apply [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] to the Quillen adjunction from step 4. Its triangle identity gives $\mathbf R\mathcal S_C(\epsilon_T)\circ\eta_{\mathbf R\mathcal S_C(T)}\simeq1$. The unit is an equivalence by step 7, so conservativity makes the counit an equivalence. Therefore the derived adjunction is an equivalence, which proves the Quillen equivalence.

source.place: Appendix A, proof of Proposition A.0.3, printed pp. 207-208 (PDF pages 214-215).

proof.text:
Each $h_y$ is cofibrant (step 2), each localized fibrant $F$ is fibrant in the simplicial localized model, and $\mathcal N_C(h_x)=N(C/x)$ (step 1). The mapping-space formula of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], the derived adjunction of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], and the unit equivalences of step 7 give
$$\operatorname{Map}^h(h_y,h_x)\simeq\operatorname{Map}^h_{/NC}(N(C/y),N(C/x)).$$
The same mapping-space formula and the explicit enriched Yoneda isomorphism of step 1 give $\operatorname{Map}^h(h_y,F)\simeq F(y)$. These are the comparisons induced by the displayed enriched adjunction: step 1 computes them on actual representable maps, while the two cited nodes give coherent naturality and compatibility with composition. Inserting the derived unit and counit therefore carries identity maps to identity maps and composition to composition with its specified homotopies. This proves every comparison and its coherence clause.
